A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable, complete versions of the same ASI paper. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–C support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, segmentation, TinyLlama–BoolQ, Raspberry Pi timing, and ablation results in Tables 1–5 and Figures 3–6.

after.justification: v2 retains original classification, segmentation, TinyLlama–BoolQ, timing, and ablation results in Tables 1–4 and Figures 3–6.

M1.justification: The rank-selection procedure, activation perplexity, warm-start subspace iteration, and compressed gradient computation remain unchanged. Fixed rank 20 for TinyLlama was already specified in v1 Table 4; v2 explains this existing adaptation.

E1.justification: Classification, segmentation, TinyLlama–BoolQ, and Raspberry Pi evaluation coverage is retained. v2 names Cityscapes pretraining and augmented Pascal VOC12 fine-tuning for the existing segmentation results; this documents Table 3 rather than establishing added coverage.

E2.justification: Deleting v1 Table 5 removes its HOSVDε reference comparison against ASI threshold-grid variants. Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged; TinyLlama already compared ASI only with vanilla training in v1.

E3.justification: The reported TinyLlama batch size changes from 128 in v1 Table 4's caption to 8 in v2 Appendix B.3, while the table entries remain identical; the PDFs do not establish a rerun. New Appendix B.2 also states epsilon > 0.4, inconsistently with the retained Section 4.1 grid that includes 0.4.

E4.justification: v2 removes Table 5's sensitivity study comparing five threshold grids through accuracy, memory, and perplexity-search time on MCUNet/Pets. The warm-start ablation and perplexity-versus-epsilon curves remain; Figure 6 is relocated and explained, not newly added.

E5.justification: There is no change in seed information, repeated-run reporting, confidence intervals, or significance testing. Both versions describe latency measurements over the first five training iterations.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain identical numerical entries, but Table 5's results disappear, including ASI accuracies of 40.78–44.06 and search times of 0.09–10.86 ms. v2 newly describes improving LLM savings with depth, although Table 4's memory-compression ratio falls from approximately 2761× at one layer to 2530× at five layers.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, Equations 1–19, and Appendix A complexity derivations are retained. Replacing some occurrences of batch-size notation Bi with B does not change the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same rank-selection and subspace-iteration contributions, including the headline 120.09× activation-memory reduction, 1.86× FLOPs reduction, and Raspberry Pi speedup claims.

C2.justification: Appendix B.3 adds interpretations of the retained segmentation and language-model results, including applicability beyond classification. It also explains that HOSVD's computational cost motivates fixed-rank compression for TinyLlama. Appendix C's backtracking scalability limitation is unchanged.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces a future code-release promise with a repository link. Appendix B.1 newly documents segmentation checkpoints, datasets, augmentation, learning rate, momentum, weight decay, batch size, and 20,000 training steps; these details concern results already present in v1.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for GPT, Gemini, BoolQ, and TinyLlama. The substantive positioning against low-rank weight adaptation, HOSVD activation compression, gradient filtering, and PowerSGD remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized language and notation edits, adds acknowledgements, and expands Appendix B with dedicated perplexity discussion and explanations of existing results. The main narrative and method exposition remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Figures 3–5 have repositioned or consolidated legends, while Figure 6 and several tables move within the document. Captions are polished and Table 5 is removed. The retained plots and table structures remain substantially the same.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reproducibility documentation through a code link and a detailed segmentation recipe, but removes the threshold-grid accuracy/search-time ablation. It also changes the stated TinyLlama batch size without explaining the unchanged results and adds a depth-scaling interpretation not clearly supported by Table 4. These documentation gains and losses of supporting evidence leave the net quality direction uncertain.
